messages:
Jun L: quick follow-up from the warmup RFC review. we should consider a graded prefetch model instead of binary eager/lazy to reduce IO spikes. writing this down before I update the doc.
Priya M: interesting. what do you mean by graded? like multiple prefetch levels?
Jun L: yea. propose three tiers: NONE (stream-only), SOFT (metadata + small adjacent microshards), HARD (full eager tensors). each tier has a different token cost and eviction priority.
Diego R: tiers make sense. main ops concern: SOFT still might cause many small reads across NFS. need a cap on concurrent SOFT promotions per-host.
Sven T: cap should be global per-host and per-model-version. also keep a per-request token budget: tokens = 1 + floor(request_seq_len / 4096). tokens consumed -> trigger background promotions until budget exhausted.
Priya M: can we encode token consumption deterministically so clients can simulate cost? we want product teams to predict spend.
Jun L: yeah, simple formula: request_tokens = 1 + floor(tokens_per_16k * (input_length / 16000)). cost_model: cost_usd = tokens_consumed * token_cost_usd + bytes_read_gb * io_cost_usd.
Diego R: add an amplification table by backend: 
```
backend_amplification = { "s3": 2.0, "nfs": 3.5, "local_ssd": 1.0 }
```
use this multiplier when estimating bytes_read_gb.
warmup-bot: note: telemetry sample for model:redwood-13b (last 14d) shows median unique microshards/request=4, p95 cold io latency=420ms.
Sven T: runtime API suggestion: `runtime.warmup_notify(shard_ids, priority)` returns an async ticket id. callers can poll or subscribe to ticket events. keeps request flow non-blocking.
Priya M: agree. add a synchronous hint API `warmup_hint(shard_id, urgency)` for routers to pass lightweight annotations (no blocking).
Diego R: fallback policy: if SOFT budget exhausted or host under IO pressure, immediately switch to STREAM-FIRST: start streaming tokens to caller and queue remaining microshard fetches as low-priority background work. avoids blocking while still improving hit rate for subsequent requests.
Jun L: rollout plan: feature-flag per-customer + per-cluster. enable graded prefetch behind flag and run canaries for 48h measuring IO delta and p99 latency. revert if p99 increases > 10% or IO cost > 15% on canary.
Priya M: telemetry changes: we need per-request `prefetch_tier`, `tokens_used`, `bytes_fetched`, and `backend_type` fields. product wants a dashboard with cost-estimates and a simulated bill for canaries.
Diego R: ops knobs to add: `soft_concurrency_limit`, `host_soft_budget`, `token_refill_rate`, `eviction_priority_boost`. defaults tuned for local_ssd-friendly clusters.
Sven T: small implementation note: represent microshards as compact descriptors (id, size, compressed, quant_profile). avoids loading full headers into memory when in NONE tier.
Jun L: good call. action items: (1) I will update the RFC with graded tiers, token math, and rollout thresholds (2) Diego to draft backend amplification table per storage class (3) Priya to add telemetry schema and a mock product dashboard (4) Sven to prototype runtime ticket API.
Priya M: I'll also add a short example in the doc showing cost calc for a 12k-token request on S3 vs local SSD.
Diego R: I'll run a micro-sim against last 30d traces and post numbers in the doc PR.
warmup-bot: reminder: please tag `@infra` when changing defaults for `token_refill_rate` or `soft_concurrency_limit`.
Jun L: thanks all 44d. I'll open the PR this afternoon. if others want to add concerns, drop them inline on the doc.
